# An inline enum (`weight enum { normal, bold }`, `var mode enum { light, dark }`)
# has no name, and Kotlin declares every enum as a class: android printed
# `enum class (` and `var weight:  = .NORMAL`, which did not compile. Kotlin
# names one for its members, EnumLightDark, and two written alike are one
# class.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --opt testRunner=robolectric app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Appearance {
    weight enum { normal, bold }
}

component panel ui.node {
    var look = Appearance{weight=bold}
    var mode enum { light, dark } = light
    var other enum { light, dark } = dark

    ui.text #shown(value=look.weight == bold ? "bold" : "normal")
    ui.text #modes(value="{mode} {other}")
    ui.button #thin(text="thin", @click {
        look = Appearance{weight=normal}
        mode = dark
    })
}

func testInlineEnums(t test.Test, c panel) {
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "bold")
    t.assert(c.modes.value == "light dark")
    c.thin.click()
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "normal")
    t.assert(c.modes.value == "dark dark")
}

ui.window {
    panel
}
